title: Professional Responsibility
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Apply the ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct: forming the lawyer–client relationship, competence, fees and client property, confidentiality and privilege, conflicts of interest, duties to courts and others, advertising and solicitation, unauthorized practice, judicial conduct, and discipline and malpractice; prepare for the MPRE.
primary_reading: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

weeks.1: Regulation of the profession and the MPRE
weeks.2: Forming and ending the lawyer–client relationship
weeks.6: The attorney–client privilege and work product
weeks.9: Duties to the court: candor and fairness
weeks.10: Duties to third parties and the public

blocks.deliverable: Decide whether a lawyer–client relationship formed in five scenarios.
Evaluate three fee agreements and a trust-account problem.
Distinguish confidentiality from privilege in four problems.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a conflict and whether informed consent cures it.
Take a timed 30-question MPRE-style set and log the misses.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Ethics opinion: answer a supplied inquiry from a law firm about a multi-issue conflict and confidentiality problem in an 1,800-word advisory opinion citing the Model Rules, then take a timed 60-question MPRE-style practice set.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
